reasons.specificity: It accurately inventories MN’s bipartisanship, regulatory control, state transformation, capital recomposition, venture-capital, and Pillar II roles, but does not deliver the requested framework-map format or worked application.
reasons.anchoring: Nearly all quoted anchors occur verbatim and substantively support their findings, though some interpretations—especially the claimed one-way explanatory direction—extend beyond the cited wording.
reasons.non_obviousness: It usefully distinguishes neoliberal mutation from neoliberal demise, bipartisanship as state form from mere consensus, and regulatory layering from abrupt institutional replacement.
reasons.coherence: The ledger, counter-evidence, and open questions consistently attribute the framework to Wijaya and Hayes and imported concepts to their named antecedents, with only a slight tension between reciprocal policy fusion and the reading’s final causal characterization.
reasons.usefulness: The inventory is strong for close reading, but it omits the requested component–relation and application–limit tables, provides no worked application, and does not lead with both visibility and a source-evidenced limit.
reasons.hallucination_risk: Most claims are bounded and source-supported, and the analysis marks the broadly Marxian profile as an inference, but it overstates the framework as directing explanation from capitalist transformation toward security policy.

decisive_errors.analysis_claim: The framework’s “explanatory direction remains from capitalist transformation toward security policy.”
decisive_errors.counter_passage: The article instead describes reciprocal causation and fusion: state transformation involves “the layering of security imperatives on economic institutions and vice versa,” and policy fusion involves “the subordination of the defence agenda to economic policy and vice versa.”

score.one_line: Source-faithful and theoretically perceptive, but only partially fulfills the requested framework-map artifact and slightly imposes a one-way causal reading on a text emphasizing reciprocal fusion.
